name: Zombie
description: Zombie is the rubber-guard arm-pummeling action that moves the opponent's hand to the mat from Mission Control so the bottom player can hug the knee and establish New York.
variant_uniqueness: Arm pummel from Mission Control to New York
summary: Zombie is the rubber-guard arm-pummeling action that moves the opponent's hand to the mat from Mission Control so the bottom player can hug the knee and establish New York.
overview:
The bottom player has broken posture and supports a high Mission Control leg. The top player's hand or forearm is still obstructing the intended arm isolation. The bottom player's free arm pummels inside to guide that hand toward the mat. Once the hand is cleared and the knee hugged, the configuration has progressed to New York.

Zombie describes an action and its arm-clearing checkpoint. The high leg controls posture while the free arm works; a half-guard lockdown on an opposing leg is a different mechanism. Terminology: Zombie arm pummel.

Maintain posture control while freeing the other arm for the pummel. Work through the opening near the hand rather than forcing a tightly clamped elbow straight outward. Guide the wrist and forearm through the available space without bending individual fingers.

Pummel slowly without finger manipulation or abrupt shoulder rotation. Support the high knee, and return to ordinary guard when the required angle is uncomfortable.

Instructional sources: [Ben Eddy — the Zombie pummel](https://www.youtube.com/watch?v=JzSxFvNA5Uo); [Brandon McCaghren — Gogoplata from rubber guard](https://www.youtube.com/watch?v=wn39-wrfsbs).
key_principles: Keep Mission Control: Maintain posture control while freeing the other arm for the pummel.
Find inside space: Work through the opening near the hand rather than forcing a tightly clamped elbow straight outward.
Move the hand to the mat: Guide the wrist and forearm through the available space without bending individual fingers.
Prevent the return pummel: Cover the cleared arm and close the knee hug as the hand reaches the mat.
Recognize New York: Once the arm is isolated, maintain that new control instead of repeatedly treating Zombie as a separate leg entanglement.
Reset a blocked attempt: Keep a safe guard and look for another opening when the opponent maintains inside frames.

top.name: Zombie Top
top.description: Zombie top perspective: Keep a useful forearm between the bodies before the bottom player gains the hand-clearing path. Move the whole arm rather than leaving the wrist exposed while the elbow remains fixed.
top.overview:
The top player is responsible for recognizing and defending the control. The bottom player has broken posture and supports a high Mission Control leg. The top player's hand or forearm is still obstructing the intended arm isolation. The bottom player's free arm pummels inside to guide that hand toward the mat. Once the hand is cleared and the knee hugged, the configuration has progressed to New York.

Keep a useful forearm between the bodies before the bottom player gains the hand-clearing path. Move the whole arm rather than leaving the wrist exposed while the elbow remains fixed. The free hand working under yours is the cue to recover inside position before the knee hug closes.

Retract the elbow toward your ribs through available space, stopping if the shoulder is caught. Raise the chest after freeing the arm and reducing the high-leg control. Do not confuse an arm pummel with lockdown defense or apply twisting leg escapes to this upper-body exchange.

bottom.name: Zombie Bottom
bottom.description: Zombie bottom perspective: Maintain posture control while freeing the other arm for the pummel. Work through the opening near the hand rather than forcing a tightly clamped elbow straight outward.
bottom.overview:
The bottom player is responsible for maintaining the control. The bottom player has broken posture and supports a high Mission Control leg. The top player's hand or forearm is still obstructing the intended arm isolation. The bottom player's free arm pummels inside to guide that hand toward the mat. Once the hand is cleared and the knee hugged, the configuration has progressed to New York.

Maintain posture control while freeing the other arm for the pummel. Work through the opening near the hand rather than forcing a tightly clamped elbow straight outward. Guide the wrist and forearm through the available space without bending individual fingers.

Cover the cleared arm and close the knee hug as the hand reaches the mat. Once the arm is isolated, maintain that new control instead of repeatedly treating Zombie as a separate leg entanglement. Keep a safe guard and look for another opening when the opponent maintains inside frames.

Zombie describes an action and its arm-clearing checkpoint. The high leg controls posture while the free arm works; a half-guard lockdown on an opposing leg is a different mechanism. Pummel slowly without finger manipulation or abrupt shoulder rotation. Support the high knee, and return to ordinary guard when the required angle is uncomfortable.

Once the pummel puts the hand outside, wrap over the cleared upper arm and hug the knee to secure the New York overhook. Keep the inside barrier as the hand travels so the top player cannot replace the lost hand post with chest pressure.
